Rajiv Ranjan Kumar vs The State Of W. B. & Ors on 6 November,
2025
Author: Suvra Ghosh

Bench: Suvra Ghosh
 16
06.11.2025
 Ct. No.26
 b.das
 Wpa 25031 of 2025
 Rajiv Ranjan Kumar
 Vs.
 The State of W. B. & Ors.

Mr. Rajdeep Majumder
 Mr. Ayan Bhattacharjee
 Mr. Moyukh Mukherjee
 Mr. A. R. Tiwari
 Ms. Priyanka Sarkar ...for the petitioner.

Mr. Pantu Deb Roy
 Mr. Pannalal Bandyopadhyay ...for the State.
Affidavit of service filed by the petitioner and report  submitted by the State are taken on record.
Heard learned counsels for the parties.
The petitioner is a developer of properties.

He is  aggrieved by the fact that series of criminal complaints are  being registered against him one after the other and he is  being tagged in a fresh complaint immediately after being  granted bail in connection with the earlier complaint.

The petitioner prayed for anticipatory bail in Rajiv Ranjan Kumar vs The State Of W. B. & Ors on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173267064/
1  connection with a complaint wherein he was sought to be  shown as arrested.

sentences.text:
By an order passed on 29th October,
 2025 in CRM (A) 3633 of 2025, a co ordinate Bench of this  Court has adjourned the prayer for showing the petitioner  as arrested in connection with the case before the learned  Court till the next date of hearing.
The interim protection  has been extended till 20th November, 2025.
2  The prayer of the petitioner is two-fold:-

First , a direction upon the State to furnish a list of cases pending against the petitioner. Second, direction upon the police authority not to take any coercive step against him in the event any further complaint is lodged.
The report submitted by the State demonstrates that 8 cases are pending against the petitioner at present.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
7. Bidhannagar East PS Case No. 72 of 2025 dated 14.09.2025 under Section 338/340(2)/318(4) of the BNS;
8. Bidhannagar North PS Case No. 113 of 2025 dated 27.10.2025 under Section 338/340(2)/351 of the BNS.
Learned counsel for the State submits, on instructions, that no other case is pending against the petitioner as on this date.
This Court is informed that the petitioner has been granted bail in 6 out of 8 cases.
He has been granted interim protection by this Court in one of the cases and is in custody in the other case.

Since it is evident from the record that several complaints are being lodged against the petitioner from 2014 till date, the police is directed to take necessary preliminary steps in accordance with law in the event any other complaint is lodged against the petitioner before taking any coercive steps against him.
With the above directions and observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall, however, be no order as to costs.
Since no affidavit is invited, the allegations contained in the writ petition are deemed not to have been admitted.
